doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

title: Improvising with Bela Fleck and Victor Wooten
summary: Lamb's first time with Bela Fleck was an hour of improvising at E-town in Boulder, where Fleck eagerly asked about his phrases.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Let me ask you about a couple of people that, according to your own resume, you have crossed paths with. Bela Fleck?

Forget about it. Amazing. You know that dude, we were playing, well I was doing this, my first experience playing with him was at it was called E-town which is a radio show, it’s like the “Prairie Home Companion” and it’s in Boulder. And so E-town had the

Flecktones and I was playing with different people. But before we had finished all the rehearsals and stuff and the stage was dark and I went over and started playing a little bit and Bela came over with his banjo and Victor Wooten came over. So we just sat there and just improvised together for about an hour. It was like — this dude — and his quest for knowledge. You know like if I was playing

something like — he’d go what? What was that? What was that phrase? You know. Whatever. He’d want to know right away and then I’d show him. And he’d go [scats] he’d go this is nice. [scats] Right? He’d start doing — but that really struck me aside from just being blown away just quietly improvising with those guys and stuff.
When you answered him what is that, you didn’t say this is a downward Lydian symmetric diminished —

Well I mean I don’t remember exactly what it was but it was something that we were vamping on a D minor 9 or whatever. So I had done something up above, I said well a half-step approach thing, so there was an answer to it. I said I think it was kind of this sort of motion based on it.
Did you hear the Flecktones Christmas CD? You should, just the “Twelve Days of Christmas” is worth.
